rationale: Atomic fitness datums emitted by phase scripts are normalized against these reference values to produce a deterministic [0.000..1.000] score. Each baseline is sourced from an industry standard, project authority, or internal observation; sourcing is non-negotiable.

baselines.source: Modern POSIX host needs >= 4GB RAM to run cc65 + ld65 + emulator concurrently. Self-hosted IIGS builds historically required >= 4MB on the IIGS itself; we measure host headroom.
baselines.citation: Apple IIGS Hardware Reference (Chapter 1) + GS/OS Reference

baselines.source: Build artifacts, ROM/disk-image mounts, and emulator state fit comfortably in 1GB headroom on the repo partition.
Phase 5 boot test requires at least one IIGS emulator (gsplus, kegs, or mame apple2gs) on PATH.
cc65 toolchain (cc65/ca65/ld65/cl65) is the 8-bit apple2enh path's required base.
cc65 v2.19+ is the current stable line; pre-2.19 lacks complete 65816/apple2enh support.
ca65 is the macro assembler shipped in the cc65 distribution.
ld65 is the linker shipped in the cc65 distribution.
cl65 is the unified compile/assemble/link driver shipped in the cc65 distribution.
A successful cc65 --target apple2enh compile of a minimal C program returns exit 0.
ca65 with the .P816 directive must accept 65816-mode source and return exit 0.
ORCA/C is the canonical 16-bit C compiler for GS/OS S16 binaries (Byte Works).
Golden Gate is Kelvin Sherlock's compatibility layer that runs ORCA tools natively on POSIX.
GSplus boots GS/OS 6.0.1 to Finder in 1-3 seconds on modern POSIX hosts.
Typical cc65 apple2enh hello world binary is 1-3 KB; 2048 is the median.
Typical ORCA/C hello world S16 with Toolbox calls is 5-10 KB; 8192 is the median.
baselines.citation: Apple IIGS Toolbox Reference Volume 1, sample programs

baselines.source: Ghidra 11.0+ is required for headless disassembly and static analysis of 65816 OMF binaries.
Ghidra 11.0+ has stable headless mode and improved decompiler output for 65816 analysis via community processor modules.
Headless Ghidra import of a valid OMF binary returns exit 0 when the import succeeds; non-zero on failure or timeout.
